  "text": "“Elian!” Peter lunged after her.

The water rose around her ankles, then her knees. Beneath the surface, something long and white darted between the stones, keeping pace. The bell rang a third time. Every ripple in the cove turned toward Elian.

She stopped and looked back at Peter. “The song,” she shouted. “It’s listening for what you remember!”

The figure’s face blurred. Its smile vanished, then returned—this time stretched across a mouth too wide for any human face.

Peter understood. It had stolen his mother’s voice, but it had not stolen the small, ordinary things that made her his mother. He shut his eyes and sang the lullaby’s first verse, badly, the way she used to when she was tired.

The figure answered with the perfect second verse.

Peter kept singing. He stumbled over the tune and left out a line. Then he made up the ending, nonsense words tumbling from his mouth. Once, his mother had done the same, and he had laughed until she laughed too.

The cove shuddered.

The figure’s song broke into a wet, grinding sound. The pale light under the water flared, revealing a chain of bells anchored to the seabed. Their clappers swung without touching, though the notes still rang.

Elian reached for the nearest rope. Peter grabbed it beside her. Together they hauled. The chain lifted, links scraping stone, and the bells gave one final, deafening note.

The figure collapsed into black water.

For a moment, only the skiff’s oars creaked. Then Ada called, “Now!”

Peter and Elian ran for shore as the cove drew back, leaving the stones bare—and the compass shining among them."
